s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
key_facts: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
patient was being treated with fluconazole
pembrolizumab treatment was stopped due to a morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption appeared different from previous reaction
patient has fever and hypotension
white blood cell count is 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count is 2940/μL
hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL
platelet count is 62 ×10^3/μL
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results were negative
respiratory viral panel and SARS-CoV-2 test results were negative

per_call: Nodal T-cell lymphoma with TFH phenotype

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy and patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash

shortlist.label: Intravascular NK-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to intravascular large B-cell lymphoma, with skin eruption and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of immunocompromise and symptoms of fever, rash, and hypotension

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy findings and patient's history of skin eruptions

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's skin eruption and history of immunocompromise

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy, as shown by hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining, is highly suggestive of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma, which is a type of lymphoma characterized by the presence of malignant cells within the blood vessels.

rejected.label: Intravascular NK-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While CD56 immunostaining is positive, which can be seen in NK-cell lymphomas, the clinical presentation and other findings are more consistent with intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with systemic symptoms, such as fever and weight loss, and is often associated with autoimmune phenomena, but the biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis, as cutaneous T-cell lymphoma typically presents with patches, plaques, or tumors that are often localized to specific areas of the skin.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with recurrent, self-healing papules or nodules, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of a widespread, asymptomatic skin eruption.
